text: Photon isn't one more Spark setting you flip. It's a native execution engine, written in C++, that replaces standard JVM execution for the operators it supports. This lesson is about which operators, and how to tell it's actually running.
Standard Spark processes rows one at a time on the JVM. Photon is vectorized native C++ — it processes a batch of rows per operator call, using CPU instructions the JVM can't reach directly.

Scans, aggregations, and joins benefit the most. Python UDFs don't benefit at all — Photon can't vectorize arbitrary Python, so that step falls back to the JVM, even inside an otherwise Photon-accelerated query.

The real check isn't the Photon checkbox on the cluster config screen — it's the query profile. Operator nodes there show a lightning-bolt Photon indicator when that specific operator actually ran on Photon.
Photon is operator-by-operator, not query-by-query. Next up: Adaptive Query Execution, which changes the plan itself at runtime.
